title: Inverse image of module sheaves is left adjoint to direct image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces, $\mathcal A$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $Y$, $\mathcal M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules, and $\mathcal N$ a sheaf of $f^{-1}\mathcal A$-modules on $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $f_p$, $f^{-1}=(f_p-)^\#$ with sheafification maps $\theta$, the unit $i$ of $f_p\dashv f_*$ on presheaves and the unit $\eta_{\mathcal A}=f_*(\theta_{\mathcal A})\circ i_{\mathcal A}:\mathcal A\to f_*f^{-1}\mathcal A$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. The inverse-image sheaf $f^{-1}\mathcal M$ is a sheaf of $f^{-1}\mathcal A$-modules: it is the sheafification of the presheaf of $f_p\mathcal A$-modules $f_p\mathcal M$ of [lem-pc-presheaf-module-inverse-image-adjunction] (1), with the $f^{-1}\mathcal A=(f_p\mathcal A)^\#$-module structure of [lem-pc-presheaf-module-sheafification-ring], the one for which $\theta_{\mathcal M}:f_p\mathcal M\to f^{-1}\mathcal M$ is semilinear over $\theta_{\mathcal A}$. The direct-image sheaf $f_*\mathcal N$, whose sections over $V\subseteq Y$ are $\mathcal N(f^{-1}V)$, is an $\mathcal A$-module through $\eta_{\mathcal A}$ ($a\in\mathcal A(V)$ acts by $\eta_{\mathcal A,V}(a)\in f^{-1}\mathcal A(f^{-1}V)$). Then the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ab}(X)}(f^{-1}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ab}(Y)}(\mathcal M,f_*\mathcal N)$ of abelian sheaves restricts to a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{f^{-1}\mathcal A}(f^{-1}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal M,f_*\mathcal N)$, natural in $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal N$.

source.place: Tag 008Y, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules (line 2933), with Tag 008X, lemma-pullback-module (line 2896), for the inverse-image module structure

proof.text: *Step 1 (the presheaf module structures).* By [lem-pc-presheaf-module-inverse-image-adjunction] (1) applied to the presheaf of rings $\mathcal O=\mathcal A$ and the presheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules $\mathcal M$, $f_p\mathcal M$ is a presheaf of $f_p\mathcal A$-modules, functorially in $\mathcal M$. By [lem-pc-presheaf-module-sheafification-ring] applied on $X$ to the presheaf of rings $f_p\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal P=f_p\mathcal M$, its abelian sheafification $f^{-1}\mathcal M=(f_p\mathcal M)^\#$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3) is a sheaf of $(f_p\mathcal A)^\#=f^{-1}\mathcal A$-modules with $\theta_{\mathcal M}$ semilinear over $\theta_{\mathcal A}$ (here $f^{-1}\mathcal A$ is the sheafification of $f_p\mathcal A$ as a presheaf of commutative rings, (3) of that definition with values in commutative rings); for $u:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'$ $\mathcal A$-linear, $f^{-1}u$ is the sheafification of the $f_p\mathcal A$-linear $f_pu$, hence $f^{-1}\mathcal A$-linear by the naturality in that lemma. This is the module structure of the statement (Stacks 008X).

source.place: Tag 008X, lemma-pullback-module, proof: 'f^{-1} is the composition of f_p and sheafification; combination of 008T and 0089'

proof.text: *Step 2 (first equality of 008Y).* Regard $\mathcal N$ as a presheaf of $f_p\mathcal A$-modules $\mathcal N_0$ through $\theta_{\mathcal A}:f_p\mathcal A\to f^{-1}\mathcal A$ (sectionwise restriction of scalars; a sheaf of $f^{-1}\mathcal A$-modules is in particular a presheaf of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]). By the universal property of [lem-pc-presheaf-module-sheafification-ring] with $\mathcal P=f_p\mathcal M$, composition with $\theta_{\mathcal M}$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{f^{-1}\mathcal A}(f^{-1}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PMod}(f_p\mathcal A)}(f_p\mathcal M,\mathcal N_0)$, natural in $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal N$; on underlying morphisms of abelian (pre)sheaves it is $\alpha\mapsto\alpha\circ\theta_{\mathcal M}$, the restriction of the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ab}(X)}(f^{-1}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PAb}(X)}(f_p\mathcal M,\mathcal N)$ of abelian sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification].

source.place: Tag 008Y, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules, proof, first equality 'by Lemma 0089'

proof.text: *Step 3 (second equality of 008Y).* By [lem-pc-presheaf-module-inverse-image-adjunction] (3) with $\mathcal O=\mathcal A$, $\mathcal G=\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal N_0$, the map $\psi\mapsto f_*\psi\circ i_{\mathcal M}$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PMod}(f_p\mathcal A)}(f_p\mathcal M,\mathcal N_0)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal A)}(\mathcal M,f_*\mathcal N_0)$, natural in $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal N_0$, where $a\in\mathcal A(V)$ acts on $f_*\mathcal N_0(V)=\mathcal N(f^{-1}V)$ through $i_{\mathcal A,V}(a)\in f_p\mathcal A(f^{-1}V)$ acting on $\mathcal N_0$, i.e. as $\theta_{\mathcal A,f^{-1}V}(i_{\mathcal A,V}(a))=\eta_{\mathcal A,V}(a)$ acting on $\mathcal N$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3). So $f_*\mathcal N_0$ is $f_*\mathcal N$ with the $\mathcal A$-module structure of the statement; it is a sheaf because $\mathcal N$ is ([def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (1)), and morphisms of sheaves of $\mathcal A$-modules $\mathcal M\to f_*\mathcal N$ are the morphisms of presheaves of $\mathcal A$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 008Y, proof, second equality 'by Lemma 008U'; the O-module structure via O -> f_*f^{-1}O from the statement of 008Y

proof.text: *Step 4 (composite; it restricts the abelian adjunction).* Composing the bijections of steps 2 and 3 gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{f^{-1}\mathcal A}(f^{-1}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal M,f_*\mathcal N)$, $\alpha\mapsto f_*(\alpha\circ\theta_{\mathcal M})\circ i_{\mathcal M}=f_*\alpha\circ(f_*\theta_{\mathcal M}\circ i_{\mathcal M})=f_*\alpha\circ\eta_{\mathcal M}$, natural in $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal N$ as a composite of natural bijections. This is the formula of the abelian adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)=\operatorname{Hom}(f_p\mathcal M,\mathcal N)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal M,f_*\mathcal N)$ of [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3), with unit $\eta_{\mathcal M}=f_*(\theta_{\mathcal M})\circ i_{\mathcal M}$; so the abelian bijection maps the $f^{-1}\mathcal A$-linear morphisms onto the $\mathcal A$-linear ones and the module bijection is its restriction.
